answer: Think of an agent economy as a shared garden: new agents start in a fenced nursery plot where they can only handle tiny jobs, and only after a long horizon of honest work do they earn keys to the main beds. Creating a hundred fake identities is cheap, but each one must tend its plot for months before it can touch real value — like planting a walnut tree and waiting years for the first nuts. The attacker pays in time and honest labor, while one betrayal burns that identity's whole plot, so flooding the garden costs far more than it can ever harvest.
